events.text: Ice-rock avalanche on the Nepali side of the border, into the Lhende Khola; seismic signal at 08:37:10
A river station stops at 08:50: Syabrubesi according to NDRRMA and the RDNA, Rasuwagadhi according to ICIMOD
Betrawati station stops transmitting; last gauge reading 3.55 m (warning 4.1 m)
Peak at Galchhi, about +8.5 m (CLaSH); maximum stage about 8.9 m (ICIMOD)
Phurke station near Malekhu above warning level
Phurke station above danger level, then swept away with its bridge
Second landslide signal; it dammed the Lhende Khola at the Chhochen confluence (the lake drained on 28 Aug)
Peak at Devghat: gauge reading 6.57 m, about 5,850 m3/s

Collapse source (CLaSH).text: A rock and ice mass failed on the Nepali side, on the north side of the Langtang Lirung massif, and fell into the Lhende Khola
Height of the head scarp: 5,000 to 5,600 m in different reports; the peer-reviewed value is 5,120 m
Fall height into the valley: about 1,000 to 1,400 m in most reports (one news report says almost 4,000 m)
Volume: about 130 to 490 million m3 by method (DEM differencing about 150, seismic inversions 200 to 490); the newest synthesis uses 132
Whether a temporary dam held for hours before the flood is disputed; USGS, CLaSH, ICIMOD and NDRRMA describe the collapse as making the flood directly

Rasuwagadhi.text: Flood at the border between 08:40 and 09:05 depending on the source; Rasuwagadhi barrage overtopped

Syabrubesi.text: A river station stopped at 08:50; NDRRMA and the RDNA name Syabrubesi, ICIMOD names Rasuwagadhi. No level was published
Copernicus damage mapping around Syabrubesi: over 240 buildings counted as destroyed, a further 32 as damaged
Peak discharge above Betrawati is unknown: no gauge survived the peak. The model starts here

Betrawati.text: Transmission stopped at 09:20 with a last gauge reading of 3.55 m (a gauge height, not a rise), below warning (4.1 m) and danger (5.0 m)

Galchhi gauge.text: Flood arrived at 10:28; peak about 10:50, +8.5 m (CLaSH) or about 8.9 m maximum stage (ICIMOD)

ICIMOD's preliminary peak is about 17,000 m3/s: the flow area of a DSM cross-section times a velocity taken from the front's travel time. ICIMOD notes the front may move faster than the water, the section is unverified and the rating is extrapolated

Malekhu.text: Phurke station: above warning at 11:26, above danger at 11:43, then lost with its bridge; Malekhu Bazaar reached about 11:50

Mugling.text: The flood had passed Mugling by 13:00 (timeline entry, no gauge level)

Devghat.text: Peak gauge reading 6.57 m at 16:00 (a gauge height, not a rise), about 5,850 m3/s; 57.4 million m3 passed between 14:10 and 18:00, 20.0 million m3 of it above the normal flow
Rise at the peak: +2.12 m above the level before the flood

toll.text: By 3 October: 1,455 recoveries of bodies and remains, 5,285 people missing (NDRRMA notes this may include unidentified bodies, rescued people and duplicates), 13,795 rescued

reported_reach.value: 7,570 affected private buildings in five districts (Rasuwa 1,779; Nuwakot 3,977; Dhading 1,451; Gorkha 263; Chitwan 100)
4,685 buildings in the satellite damage mapping of 5 Sep
37 motorable bridges (33 washed out, 4 partly damaged) and 68 trail bridge spans
13 projects, 759 MW (7 in operation, 6 under construction)
Mapped affected land in the assessed wards: Rasuwa 1,926 ha, Nuwakot 1,100 ha

reported_rise._note: Reported rise of the water above the level before the flood, for the place card's range bar (the facts with their sources are under places)
